title: Write Arrange/Act/Assert tests that kill six mutants
problem: app.py is a working messages API (send, list, delete messages in chats 1 and 2). This time you write the tests. Fill in the five test functions in test_messages.py using the client fixture. test_meta.py runs your tests against six copies of app.py, each with one realistic bug, and every bug must make at least one of your tests fail.
requirements: Edit only test_messages.py. Don't change app.py, conftest.py or test_meta.py
Keep the five test names; each test takes only the client fixture
Structure each test as Arrange / Act / Assert (blank lines or comments between the parts)
Every test asserts the status code, and asserts on the body where the spec fixes it
All your tests pass on the real app.py
Write your tests from the docstrings and app.py first. Read the mutants in test_meta.py only after your first run
contract: test_messages.py defines test_send_message_returns_201_and_the_message, test_send_to_unknown_chat_is_404, test_blank_text_is_422, test_list_shows_only_this_chat and test_list_keeps_sending_order, each taking (client)
expectedBehavior: pytest -q shows your five tests and all six test_tests_kill[...] cases passing
edgeCases: A field in the response that your test never checks lets a bug in that field through
A chat that has no messages while another chat has some
Order of a list with two or more items
hints: Conceptual: a test only protects what it asserts. For each test, ask: which wrong response would still pass my asserts? If 200 instead of 201 would pass, or chat_id 1 instead of 2, add the assert that rules it out.

Specific: the docstrings pick the chat for a reason. Posting to chat 2 and asserting chat_id == 2 catches a handler that hard-codes chat 1. For the 'only this chat' test, the Arrange step must put a message in the OTHER chat first.

Implementation: Arrange builds the input (and sends setup requests); Act is one client.post/get call stored in response; Assert checks response.status_code first, then response.json(). For 422 tests, assert on response.json()["detail"][0]["loc"], not on the message text.
evaluation: All 11 tests pass, including all six test_tests_kill cases
Each test has one Act step and visible Arrange/Act/Assert parts
Status code asserted in every test; body asserted where the spec fixes it
You can say which of your tests kills each mutant
